title: ¿Por qué se hundió el Titanic si decían que era insumergible? 🚢
staging_mode_proposal: stage: the liner on a sea slab on the Coral stage, the hull turning x-ray to show its compartments. Not cutaway: with 019, 022 and 024 cutaway, a cutaway 026 would put four cutaways in the five productions 019-026 (format policy rotation).
curiosity_reason: The most famous shipwreck; the 'unsinkable' question is carried by nearly everyone; dangerous. Fame evidence in the bank entry.
hook_question: ¿Por qué se hundió el Titanic si decían que era insumergible?
false_belief: El iceberg le abrió un agujero gigante en el casco.
turn: Scene 5: the walls between the compartments did not reach the top, so as the bow went down the water spilled over each wall into the next compartment.
closing_reframe: Al Titanic no lo hundió un agujero gigante: lo hundieron unas paredes sin techo.
share_archetype: ese amigo que lleva la cubeta de hielo llena hasta el borde

description:
¿Por qué se hundió el Titanic si decían que era insumergible? No fue un agujero gigante: el iceberg dejó unas rendijas finas.
Las paredes de adentro no llegaban hasta arriba, y el agua se desbordó de un compartimento al siguiente. 🚢
Envíaselo a ese amigo que lleva la cubeta de hielo llena hasta el borde.
wardrobe: No figure on screen (Historia: people stay off screen; no human-figure staging is needed for this story).

scenes.name: hook
scenes.narration: ¿Por qué se hundió el Titanic si decían que era insumergible? Casi todos creen que el iceberg le abrió un agujero gigante en el casco.
scenes.what_changes: Night on the stage: the liner steams across the sea slab, smoke trailing from its funnels; a faceted iceberg slides in ahead of the bow; the tag ¿AGUJERO GIGANTE? hangs over the bow.
scenes.transformation: barco navegando tranquilo → aparece el iceberg delante de la proa
scenes.camera: travelling lateral junto al barco, de popa a proa

elements.name: ocean liner afloat at sea
elements.route: library ocean-liner (sealed, titanic_rig.Liner) on a sea slab
elements.risk: low: sealed asset, read 88/90/90 alone; the sea slab is new context

elements.name: iceberg ahead of a ship
elements.route: build: faceted low-poly ice mass, pale blue-white, most of it below the sea slab (seen through the translucent sea)

scenes.name: diseno
scenes.narration: Sus constructores lo habían pensado: quince paredes de acero partían el casco en dieciséis compartimentos. Con los cuatro primeros inundados, seguía flotando.
scenes.what_changes: The hull turns x-ray: fifteen steel walls rise one by one across it and split it into sixteen boxes; then the first four boxes at the bow fill with water and the ship settles a little, still afloat.
scenes.transformation: casco hueco → quince paredes lo dividen; cuatro compartimentos se llenan y el barco sigue a flote
scenes.camera: órbita alta sobre el casco mientras suben las paredes, y bajada a la línea de flotación

elements.name: ship hull divided into compartments by walls (x-ray)
elements.route: library ocean-liner in an x-ray state: translucent shell, opaque walls and floor (titanic_rig cutaway state re-staged as x-ray, not a sealed pose)
elements.risk: medium-high: an x-ray hull may read as a 'rack' or 'tray'; the funnels and bow shape are the cue; proof P2

scenes.name: choque
scenes.narration: La noche del catorce de abril de mil novecientos doce, el iceberg solo rozó el costado de la proa. No abrió un agujero: dejó una hilera de rendijas finas que, sumadas, medían como un metro cuadrado.
scenes.what_changes: The iceberg scrapes along the starboard bow; plates buckle and a row of thin bright slits opens one after another along the waterline; a small square (one square metre, to scale) assembles beside the hull from the slits' total area.
scenes.transformation: casco intacto → una hilera de rendijas finas a lo largo de la proa
scenes.camera: seguimiento rasante del roce, de proa hacia atrás, con un retroceso al final

elements.name: iceberg scraping the side of a ship
elements.route: ocean-liner + iceberg build; slits as emissive accent cuts on the bow plates
elements.risk: medium: proof P1 covers the iceberg beside the bow; the scrape is the event

scenes.name: cinco
scenes.narration: Pero las rendijas recorrían la proa, y el agua entró en al menos cinco compartimentos a la vez. Uno más de los que el barco aguantaba.
scenes.what_changes: Inside the x-ray hull, water jets in through the slits and five bow boxes fill together; the fifth box lights in the error colour; the bow starts to dip.
scenes.transformation: cuatro compartimentos que aguantaba → cinco llenos, la proa empieza a bajar
scenes.camera: empuje dentro del casco a lo largo de los compartimentos de proa
overlays_plan: mark red on the fifth compartment at 'uno'

elements.name: water flooding the front compartments of a ship
elements.route: ocean-liner x-ray state; water as a physically based blue material rising in the boxes

scenes.name: desborde
scenes.narration: Y aquí estaba el problema: las paredes no llegaban hasta arriba. Con la proa hundiéndose, el agua pasó por encima de cada una al compartimento siguiente, como en una cubeta de hielo inclinada.
scenes.what_changes: The turn: the bow tilts down; the water in the full bow boxes climbs to the open wall tops and pours over each one into the next box, then the next; beside the ship, an ice-cube tray tilts the same way and spills cube to cube.
scenes.transformation: agua contenida en la proa → se desborda por encima de cada pared hacia atrás
scenes.camera: travelling a lo largo de los bordes de las paredes, siguiendo el agua de un compartimento al siguiente
overlays_plan: label SIN TECHO tag with leader to a wall top at 'arriba'

elements.name: water spilling over the walls inside a tilted ship
elements.route: ocean-liner x-ray state tilted bow-down; water sheets pouring over the wall tops
elements.risk: high: the turn of the story and an event element; proof P3

elements.name: tilted ice-cube tray spilling water
elements.route: build: geometric plastic tray, water material in the cells
elements.risk: low-medium: a tray with water reads; secondary element, read with the scene

scenes.name: final
scenes.narration: Uno a uno, los compartimentos se fueron llenando. Dos horas y cuarenta minutos después del choque, el Titanic se hundió, y murieron unas mil quinientas personas.
scenes.what_changes: The boxes fill in order from bow to stern; the stern rises out of the sea slab, the lights on the decks go out, and the whole liner slides under the sea line, leaving the slab's surface empty.
scenes.transformation: barco medio inundado → se llena entero y desaparece bajo el mar
scenes.camera: retroceso amplio y lento mientras el barco se inclina y se hunde

elements.name: ocean liner sinking stern up
elements.route: ocean-liner (sealed) animated down through the sea slab

scenes.name: cierre
scenes.narration: Así que al Titanic no lo hundió un agujero gigante: lo hundieron unas paredes sin techo. Envíaselo a ese amigo que lleva la cubeta de hielo llena hasta el borde.
scenes.what_changes: Single reframe image: the hull rises back into view as an x-ray, every open wall top lighting in the accent one after another, the row of open tops that did it; the camera pulls back.
scenes.transformation: barco hundido → el casco vuelve a aparecer con los bordes abiertos de sus paredes encendidos
scenes.camera: retroceso desde los bordes de las paredes hasta el barco entero

sources: Sixteen watertight compartments divided by fifteen transverse bulkheads: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Titanic'; British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry, testimony of Edward Wilding (titanicinquiry.org).

Flooding threshold. FLAGGED (confirm the wording at the beat sheet): 'could stay afloat with the first four compartments flooded' (Wikipedia 'RMS Titanic'; Titanic Wiki 'Watertight Bulkheads': afloat with 3 flooded or the forward 4, sinks with 5 or more); the US Senate report gives 'any two main compartments' as the safe case. The narration says 'con los cuatro primeros inundados, seguía flotando', which matches the forward-four case and does not claim any four.

The walls did not reach the top: US Senate Inquiry report (titanicinquiry.org AmInqRep05): only the first bulkhead reached C deck, several reached D, bulkheads 3-9 ended at E deck, and the non-watertight E deck is why the compartments failed; water spilled over the tops into the next compartment (same report; Britannica).

The damage: six thin openings along the starboard hull totalling about 12-13 square feet (Deseret News 1997-04-08 'Did small holes in hull doom Titanic', reporting the 1996 sonar survey) or 'one square meter (12 square feet)' (NIST, 'NIST reveals how tiny rivets doomed Titanic vessel'); Wilding's 1912 equivalent opening of 12 square feet (Encyclopedia Titanica, 'Somewhere about 12 square feet'). Spoken as 'como un metro cuadrado'. The slit count is not spoken or shown as a number.

Compartments breached: 'at least five' (Britannica); six of sixteen in other accounts. Spoken as 'al menos cinco'; 'uno más de los que el barco aguantaba' follows from the forward-four threshold above (FLAGGED with it).

Collision about 11:40 p.m. on 14 April 1912; sinking about 2:20 a.m. on 15 April: about two hours and forty minutes (British Wreck Commissioner's Inquiry via Live Science 'The Titanic: the true story behind the unsinkable ship'). Spoken as 'dos horas y cuarenta minutos'.
About 1,500 people died: Encyclopaedia Britannica 'Titanic'. Spoken as 'unas mil quinientas personas'.
Not used: the survivor count, the lifeboat shortage, the rivet-metallurgy debate and any quotation of the 'unsinkable' wording (separate stories, not this mechanism).
simplifications: The liner is the stylised library model with no livery or name; the hull is shown as an x-ray with the walls simplified to equal-height open boxes (in reality the walls stopped at E or D deck, the first at C).
The water in each box keeps a level surface when the ship pitches; the order of filling is staged, not simulated.
The ice-cube tray is an analogy object beside the ship, not a scale model.

historia_checks.one_complete_story: From the design to the sinking and the death toll; the outcome is told (scene 6) before the reframe (scene 7). Not serialized.
historia_checks.mechanism_heart: Remove the mechanism sentences (the walls and compartments, the four-compartment limit, the thin slits, the spill over the wall tops) and only 'it hit an iceberg and sank' remains: the story does not stand without them. PASS.
historia_checks.people: No person on screen; the builders and the dead are named in narration only.

flatness_test: 1. hook: the liner sails on and an iceberg appears ahead of its bow.
2. diseno: fifteen walls rise and split the hull; four bow boxes flood and the ship still floats.
3. choque: the iceberg scrapes the bow and a row of thin slits opens; their total area forms a one-square-metre tile.
4. cinco: water floods five bow boxes at once; the fifth lights red and the bow dips.
5. desborde: the bow tilts and water pours over each open wall top into the next box (turn).
6. final: the boxes fill to the stern and the liner slides under the sea.
7. cierre: the hull returns as an x-ray with every open wall top lit.
